candidates.statement: (hereafter applicants ) who are required to conduct postmarketing studies or clinical trials under 19 section 505(o)(3) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). 3 These 20 postmarketing studies and clinical trials are also commonly referred to as postmarketing 21 requirements (PMRs), or 505(o)(3) PMRs (hereafter PMRs ). An applicant required to conduct a 22 PMR under section 505(o)(3) must provide certain information to FDA, including a timetable for 23 study or clinical trial completion and periodic reports on the status of the study or clinical trial. 24 If an applicant fails to comply with the timetable or other requirements of section 25 505(o)(3)(E)(ii), the applicant is in violation of section 505(o)(3), unless the applicant has 26 demonstrated good cause for its noncompliance or other violation. 4

candidates.statement: Section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii) of the FD&C Act requires an applicant to periodically report on the 94 status of each PMR. 13 To comply with section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii), the applicant must also report on 95 the status of any other study or clinical trial undertaken to investigate a safety issue. Except 96 when otherwise provided, FDA considers the submission of the annual report required under 21 97 CFR 314.81 or 21 CFR 601.70, as applicable, as satisfying this periodic reporting requirement, if 98 the required elements of information about the status of the PMR set forth in 505(o)(3)(E)(ii) are 99 included in that report. 14
candidates.context: A PMR timetable may include additional milestones, including interim milestones. 92 If an applicant fails to meet one or more of the milestones specified in the timetable or fails to 102 submit periodic reports on the status of the PMR(s), FDA considers the applicant to be in 103 violation of section 505(o)(3) of the FD&C Act, unless the applicant has demonstrated good 104 cause for its PMR noncompliance. Under section 505(o)(3)(E)(ii), FDA is responsible for 105 determining what constitutes good cause for PMR noncompliance. FDA makes this 106 determination by evaluating an applicant’s explanation of the circumstance(s) that led to the 107 noncompliance and any other information deemed pertinent. candidates.statement: Because the required milestone may occur far in advance of the required periodic updates that 289 are generally submitted in an annual report, FDA strongly encourages applicants to proactively 290 inform FDA about the progress and status of their PMR(s). If an applicant anticipates missing a 291 milestone or has already missed the milestone and submission of an annual report is not 292 imminent, FDA encourages the applicant to notify FDA as soon as possible of the delay and 293 submit thorough explanations of the failure to meet the PMR milestones. Applicants who have a 294 revised PMR timetable who fail or anticipate failing to meet any of the revised milestones should 295 also submit an explanation for FDA to evaluate. As more fully discussed below, applicants who 296 miss (or anticipate missing) PMR milestones should promptly implement the appropriate actions 297 that are necessary to correct the underlying circumstance(s) of the PMR noncompliance and 298 include a description of these actions in the explanation for PMR noncompliance. 299
candidates.context: B. Submitting an Explanation for PMR Noncompliance or Anticipated 286 Noncompliance 287 FDA determines whether an applicant has demonstrated good cause for noncompliance with a 301 PMR milestone in the timetable only after the applicant has missed the milestone date. FDA 302 recognizes, however, that an applicant can often know in advance that a milestone may be 303 missed, proactively notify FDA of the anticipated missed milestone, and provide an explanation 304 for the anticipated delay. Before the applicant misses a milestone, FDA can assess whether it 305 finds that the applicant has provided sufficient justification for the anticipated delay (i.e., 306 anticipated failure to meet a future milestone). FDA plans to notify an applicant of its 307 determination that an applicant has failed to provide sufficient justification for the anticipated 308 delay in meeting the PMR milestone. 30

candidates.statement: Applicants should identify their submitted explanations for actual or anticipated PMR delay with 311 the following wording in bold capital letters on the top of the first page of the submission: 312 “Notification of Failure to Meet a PMR Milestone(s) Required Under Section 505(o)” or 313 “Notification of Anticipated Failure to Meet a PMR Milestone(s) Required Under Section 314 505(o).” 315
